extracted.intended_audience: writers/authors preparing to pitch to literary agents
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and delivering a tight, well-rehearsed 30-second elevator pitch to literary agents, covering what to say, how to present credentials, and how to prompt next steps. Targets in-person pitches but applies generally to agent-facing pitches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elevator pitch length and readiness
rubrics_metrics.description: You must be prepared to pitch your idea in 30 seconds or fewer (this is called an “Elevator Pitch”).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Produce a tight, well-rehearsed pitch; commit a few key sentences to memory so you never waste an opportunity. Agents have limited time — rehearse so your pitch fits the 30-second constraint and sounds natural rather than rambling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tell the literary agent who you are
rubrics_metrics.description: State your name and job title, or the title of the position you're seeking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduce yourself briefly and clearly. Example given: “Hi, my name is Miranda Mechanic, and I’m a licensed automotive mechanic who writes how-to articles for women who don’t want their cars to get the best of them.” Keep this succinct and relevant to the pitch.

rubrics_metrics.name: State what you want
rubrics_metrics.description: Literary agents want to know what you want — don’t beat around the bush. State what you’re after.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be direct about your objective (e.g., placement of an article, representation for a novel). Example: “I’m interested in placing some of my articles with your magazine, Auto Care for Everybody.” Clear goals guide the agent’s response and next steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show why you’re the best choice
rubrics_metrics.description: List any degrees, writing credentials, training or experience that relate to what you’re seeking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide brief, relevant qualifications that support your stated goal. Ensure qualifications match the objective (don’t list unrelated credentials). If you lack direct experience, name transferable qualities or skills (attention to detail, passion, etc.). Aim for a memorable single detail that separates you from others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give a call to action
rubrics_metrics.description: Give literary agents a call to action — ask for what you want so the interaction can continue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conclude by requesting a next step (showing clips, leaving contact info, arranging to send materials). Example: “I’d like to show you copies of my articles, including ‘How to Change a Tire When It’s Twenty Below Zero’ and ‘How to Add Oil When You’re Wearing a Power Suit.’” The call to action is what leads to further interaction — don’t omit it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailor pitch to agent type/market
rubrics_metrics.description: Craft your pitch with awareness of the agent’s market and specialization (New York vs. London, children’s vs. Christian, established vs. new agents).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust wording, examples, and emphasized credentials to suit the agent’s focus and market. The page emphasizes that whether pitching to any kind of literary agent, crafting a few key sentences targeted to them and committing them to memory gives you a better chance of success.
